title: Crypto & Security Engine: AES-128 (FIPS-197) ECB encrypt and decrypt, key written as four words, one round per clock

words.name: KEY0
words.desc: key bits [127:96] (write only; reset 0); a write while busy is refused (PROTOCOL)

fields.desc: the 128-bit block taken by START (plaintext to encrypt, ciphertext to decrypt)
write 1: run one block with the current key, DIN and CTRL (21 clocks); refused while busy (PROTOCOL)
the 128-bit result of the last operation, valid from DONE
an operation is running (key expansion, then the rounds)

irqs.name: DONE
irqs.desc: an operation finished; DOUT holds the result

irqs.name: PROTOCOL
irqs.desc: START or a KEY write while busy (refused)

notes: Wide values are little-endian across words: DIN0 and DOUT0 hold bits [31:0], DIN3 and DOUT3 bits [127:96]. The key is the other way round: KEY0 holds bits [127:96], as the core takes it.
The key words are write only (the core keeps no read path to them) and take whole words: a KEY write with PSTRB != 4'hF gets PSLVERR and is dropped.
